about: Company foundations, entered by hand. Each entry names a foundation by EIN (it must be in the IRS data), the company behind it, and, where the company's own giving page says so, the program a small nonprofit can apply to. serves lists the states a national program is open in ("*" for every state), so the foundation is shown there even when its IRS return lists other states. grantmatch/corporate.py checks this file. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

program.name: Spark Good local grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) public charities, government entities, schools and faith-based groups with community-benefit projects, serving the same area as the Walmart store, Sam's Club or distribution center they ask. Needs a Spark Good account on Walmart.com, verified by Deed. 501(c)(4), (c)(6) and (c)(19) groups can't apply.
program.when: Three cycles a year: February 1 to April 15, May 1 to July 15, and August 1 to December 31 (one line on the page says November 30; confirm there). One grant per store or club per year.
program.how: Apply through your Spark Good account at walmart.com/nonprofits, choosing the nearby store, club or distribution center.
program.focus: Local needs, such as hunger relief, economic opportunity, sustainability, disaster response and community connection

program.name: Publix Super Markets Charities requests
program.who: Nonprofits that operate or serve clients in Florida, Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia or Kentucky. A staff or board member registers the organization.
program.when: Hunger relief requests March 1 to April 30 (decisions in September); housing and shelter requests July 1 to August 31 (decisions at year end); other requests any time.
program.how: Register once, and update yearly, on the Publix Charitable Donations site (charitabledonations.publix.com).
program.focus: Youth, education, hunger, homelessness and stronger communities

program.name: Truist Foundation grants
program.who: 501(c)(3) public charities in the United States, or applicants through a fiscal sponsor. Not for annual, scholarship or general operating requests. Three years between grants.
program.amount: At least $15,000 for local and regional grants
program.when: Deadlines March 31, July 31 and November 30 each year, with decisions about four months later.
program.how: Online portal from the foundation's grant application page, after an eligibility quiz.
program.focus: Career pathways for adults into middle-skill jobs, and support for small businesses

program.name: TD Charitable Foundation regional grants
program.who: Nonprofits in TD Bank's communities; Florida has its own giving contact. The eligibility rules are in the regional grants FAQ.
program.when: 2027 deadlines: March 12, May 14 and July 30, with decisions about two months later.
program.how: Online application through CyberGrants, from TD's funding opportunities page.
program.focus: Quality of life in TD's communities, including affordable housing and nonprofit capacity building
